# AI Engineering

> A course in AI engineering that takes a reader from nothing installed through
> to building and measuring a working system. It runs on the Python standard
> library alone: no account, no API key, no GPU, no paid service, and no
> network access at any point.

The course exists because the popular alternatives stop working. They depend on
services that are retired, datasets that are withdrawn and libraries that move,
and their material is written faster than it can be checked. This one is built
so that it cannot decay unnoticed.

## What is guaranteed, and how

- Every lesson runs. Every solution and check is executed on Linux, macOS and
  Windows on each change, and again nightly.
- Every number shown in a lesson is generated by the code beside it and
  compared against the real output, never typed by hand.
- Nothing outside the Python standard library is imported anywhere in the
  course, and that is enforced by a program rather than by a policy.
- Lessons run with the network closed, so a lesson cannot come to depend on
  something that can be taken away.
- Every solution prints the same thing on every run. Each one is executed under
  three different string hash seeds and the output must match, so no figure in
  the course can depend on a clock, on unseeded randomness, or on the order a
  set happens to have.

## Structure

- phases/ holds the course, one directory per phase, one per lesson inside it.
- Each lesson is three files: README.md teaches it, solve.py is the worked
  solution, check.py decides whether the result is right.
- tools/ holds the five programs that enforce the guarantees above, and they
  can be run by anybody: run_lessons.py, check_output.py, check_imports.py,
  check_determinism.py and check_glossary.py.
- The course is 45 lessons across 9 phases, about 33 hours by the estimates at
  the top of each phase, and builds one system throughout rather than a set of
  disconnected exercises.
